description:

comments.author: claude-coordinator:shady2k@mbp:main#45620410
comments.text:
Handoff 2026-09-24

## Do this first
Present the preflight below to the owner again (in Russian, briefly) and ask for acceptance as a whole or changes by item; on acceptance run take-task on this task. The owner declined to start today only because of the 2-3 h estimate.

## Decisions (proposed in the preflight, NOT yet accepted by the owner)
1. Evidence level: records (no CI); records are trusted, not verified; say so in the integration.
2. Change format: docs/changes/<id>/change.md per the skills' template, plus full proposed capability files docs/changes/<id>/capabilities/<name>.md; the adapter computes deltas by comparing them with the current capability at the target revision (no hand-written deltas). Coverage and preserves as bullet lines '- <capability>/<requirement>: <check ids | reason>'.
3. Catalogue: docs/system/index.md ('no coverage yet') and an empty capabilities/ directory; no invented sample capability (departure from documents.md's seed advice, justified by 'no empty scaffolds' and 'first change may add against an absent baseline').
4. Enforcement in the commit-msg hook: every commit -> product phase; a commit touching product code (outside docs/, .shady2k/, .beads/, .githooks/, root *.md) -> its linked task must belong to a change passing the feature phase; a commit touching docs/system/capabilities/ -> close phase; stage acceptance -> acceptance phase run by take-task as a command.
5. Policy: behavior/no-behavior owe static, test, mutation, review; supporting owes review plus the tooling's own tests; commands for static/test arrive with the first code (foundation feature madarch-ozp).
6. requireApproval: true for behavior changes; approval is one sentence in the preflight, recorded as the owner's words; changeDigest per documents.md.
7. Evidence storage: tracker comments on the change's tasks, first line 'check: {id,status,reference}' or 'approval: {changeDigest,reference}'.
8. Exemptions: none needed (no open task has code); this task is a supporting change.
9. Write both sentences into the integration: local hooks are feedback, not a boundary (--no-verify bypasses them); a refusal is owed work whoever could walk past it.
Estimate: 2-3 h agent work (a guess: no run history). Run mode: inline in the owner's session. Review: same-model independent reviewer, disclosed (Codex MCP was not connected).

## Not recorded elsewhere (verified)
- docs/vision.md and docs/milestones/mvp.md parse with document-format.mjs's section lists (their ## headings match parseVision/parseMilestone exactly; checked by reading).
- runs.mjs pace: 'Too little history ... any estimate is a guess'; no open or stalled runs.

## Traps
- In shells whose snapshot predates 2026-09-23, 'br' is still the removed broot function: call the tracker as 'command br'. New shells are fine.

## Where things are
- Contract: the skills' setup-shady2k-skills/documents.md (Executable contract, Boundaries and recovery); checker and parsers already copied to .shady2k/checks/.
- Merged local branches setup/shady2k-skills and docs/vision-and-decisions can be deleted (owner not asked yet).

title: Connect a fresh clone with one committed command and sign commits with the owner's public email
description:
Found while connecting a clone on the owner's second computer (2026-09-24).

## Owner decision
Commits are signed with the owner's public email (the one shown on the GitHub profile), not the GitHub noreply address: it is already public, so hiding it buys nothing. The integration's rule 'Commits use the GitHub noreply address' and the fresh-clone step 'set user.email to the noreply address' change accordingly. Past noreply commits stay as they are.

## Problems
- Connecting a fresh clone is six manual steps listed in .shady2k/integration.md (hooks path, the br-portable-path filter, private patterns, br import and source-path migration). Git never applies repository config on clone, so this cannot be automatic, but it can be one committed command.
- The private pattern list lives only in .git/info/private-patterns of each clone, so a second machine starts without it.
- .githooks/privacy-guard.sh exits 0 when that file is missing: an unconnected clone passes any staged content silently.

## Done when
- one committed command connects a fresh clone (hooks path, filter, br import and path migration, private patterns) and is idempotent on a connected one;
- the guard reads patterns from .git/info/private-patterns and from a documented per-user location outside the repository (synced by the owner), and refuses a commit, saying how to connect, when neither exists;
- the integration states the public-email rule and names the command as the fresh-clone step;
- proved on a fresh clone: before connecting, a commit is refused with the connect hint; after connecting, the hooks reject planted violations.

## Left out
No global git config is written by the command; syncing the pattern file between machines is the owner's own tooling.
